item.title: Cotter Caves
item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave
  • Source: Google

Access and warnings

Site closed for Bat Conservation

Additional Notes

There seems to be confusion here. There is the caves side and on the other side of the small valley is the mine side. When standing at the road adjacent to the river look up the small valley. The walkway and steps to the left go to the cave which is fenced off. Above this are two more smaller caves entrances. On the right hand side of the valley is a small track taking you through the old mullock dump and along to where the old mine is. Railway lines can still be seen going into the collapsed entrance to the adit. In the 90s this went back about 20m or so but was flooded. The mine is at the top of the valley and nowhere near the caves.

item.title: Lennox House Cave - Location TBC
item.description:
Details

Identification

  • Feature type: Cave
  • System name: Lake Burley Griffin
  • Source: ABC

Cave and exploration data

  • Goes to water: Yes

Additional Notes

“The only mapped and formerly accessible cave within central Canberra is located below the Acton foreshore of Lake Burley Griffin. The Lennox House cave is around eight metres deep and it was once used as a rubbish tip. The name references the nearby historic Lennox House and Lennox Crossing. The cave was submerged when the lake was created by damming the Molonglo River in 1963.”
